# Go Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a patterns skill for writing and reviewing Go the way the language wants to be written. Its core philosophy is that Go favors simplicity over cleverness: code should be obvious on first read. You get the zero-value discipline (design types so they work without constructors), explicit error handling with wrapped context instead of clever control flow, small interfaces defined where they are used rather than where they are implemented, and package layout guidance that keeps dependencies pointing inward. Each principle comes with good/bad pairs, including the classic traps like unnecessary closures, ignored errors, and interfaces declared too early. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; the simplicity-first stance can feel restrictive if your team likes abstraction-heavy designs; examples assume a reasonably modern Go toolchain. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
